subject: Post-call: concurrency & streaming SLOs — recap + next steps
content:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: concurrency & streaming SLOs — recap + next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can size a POC and a dedicated capacity proposal: 

Call recap (short)
- Goal: embed streaming responses into customer-facing flows (real-time summaries + TTS pipeline).
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 250ms for responses up to 512 tokens; p99 negotiated if we add dedicated capacity.
- Streaming: ~60% of requests will use streaming; client expects first-chunk <= 200ms after request start and subsequent deltas every <= 150ms for ~6–10 chunks.
- Throughput: sustained baseline ~30 req/s with payloads up to 512 tokens; burst up to 150 req/s for up to 60s during peak events.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent active requests ~40 (average) but can spike to 70 briefly during campaigns.
- Connection pooling: client-side pool expected to maintain ~25 keepalive connections (HTTP/2 preferred).
- Max sequence length: up to 1024 tokens for some workflows.
- Security: IP allowlist + TLS mutual auth will be required; procurement will need SOC2 artifact set.

Clarifying questions for sizing (please reply inline):
1) Typical session duration (avg tokens per session / minutes per session)?
2) Fraction of traffic that is streaming vs non-streaming (you said ~60% but confirm).
3) Any strict regional constraint for data residency?
4) Is the client open to a short Dedicated pool (2–4 week POC) to validate tail latency?

Next steps I propose:
- We produce a Dedicated POC plan and a rate-limit/connection guidance doc (we start with a conservative pool config + burst policy).
- We share a draft commercial quote and a proposed meet to review technical configs (30–45m).

Attachments: call recording stub (call-recording-20280719.mp3).

Thanks — I copied Karthik and Ben to scope the technical and commercial asks.

Best,
Marissa Cole

> 2) Fraction of traffic streaming vs non-streaming?
Confirming ~60% streaming, 40% standard non-streaming completion calls.

Primary region: US (west coast), but we need EU availability later this year (FYI).

Procurement is open to a short POC but we need an estimated monthly that isolates the burst window. They also want a simple failover plan if Dedicated capacity drops below target.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: concurrency & streaming SLOs — tech sizing notes

Hi all — quick technical notes and a recommended configuration from engineering based on the numbers Marissa summarized and Sara confirmed. Quoted as plain guidance for sizing a Dedicated POC: 

1) Request concurrency and connection pooling
- Client-side: 25 keepalive connections is fine if client uses HTTP/2 multiplexing; that will support ~10x logical streams per TCP connection depending on client impl, so we recommend configuring server-side connection limits for 200 concurrent streams to avoid head-of-line issues.
- Recommended initial server pool: 32 persistent worker connections per customer (with HTTP/2 multiplexing enabled). That maps to ~320 concurrent streams as a safe ceiling.

2) Burst handling and graceful degradation
- For 150 req/s 60s bursts: recommend a combination of reserved burst capacity + short-lived queueing (max queue 3s) and a soft-fail fallback that uses a smaller model variant if latency or token rate limits are hit. We can offer an isolated burst credit for the POC (one-time buffer) or include permanent burst allowances at a price.

3) Throughput & token budget
- With 30 sustained req/s @ up to 512 tokens avg, expect ~15k tokens/sec or ~54M tokens/hour. That will need a Dedicated plan sized for ~60M tokens/hour to keep headroom.

4) Streaming specifics
- To hit first-chunk <=200ms we need a model with small initial prompt compile time and a warm KV cache for common prefixes. Recommend a short warmup period in POC with synthetic traffic.

5) Failover / region
- We can configure regional fallback to a compatible model in another region but that adds ~50–120ms extra latency; still acceptable for availability fallback but not for p95 SLA.

6) Practical recommendation (POC config)
- Dedicated pool: 2 x A100-style nodes (or equivalent) reserved for 2 weeks; autoscale policy: allow temporary +50% burst via credits; server pool: 32 worker connections + HTTP/2 multiplexing; queueing: 3s max; fallback model: smaller quantized variant.
- Connection & token limits: base rate limit 30 req/s sustained, burst up to 150 req/s via credits, per-tenant concurrent stream cap 320.

I attached our concurrency guidelines and current Q3 ratecard for commercial. Happy to walk through these with your infra team.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
